hypothesis.statement: The discriminator between `speech` (copy) and `formats` (direct) is the SIZE/TYPE of the pointed-to object rather than anything about the declaration: `formats` is `char*` into a byte pool and `speech` is a pointer to a 0x5E4-byte struct whose accesses carry displacements up to 0x564+, so the address web feeding the big-displacement loads may be classified differently by the allocator. Test it by giving `speech` a type whose accesses need only small displacements (e.g. keep the record but reach the boss table through a second, separately-based pointer) and watching whether the +0x40 `mr` moves.

attributes.probed_form:
THE POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST, because it is what justified reopening. In THIS function's prologue, ONE INSTRUCTION APART, two file-scope addresses are lowered into callee-saved homes and only one pays the copy:
  T 30: lis r3,sSpeechNameBuf@ha   O 30: lis r3,sSpeechNameBuf@ha
  T 34: addi r30,r3,@lo   <-DIRECT  O 34: addi r0,r3,@lo  <-via r0
  T 3c: lis r3,lbl_80114A48@ha     O 3c: lis r3,lbl_80114A48@ha
                                   O 40: mr r26,r0   <- THE SURPLUS
  T 40: addi r31,r3,@lo   <-DIRECT  O 44: addi r30,r3,@lo <-DIRECT
So OUR OWN compiler emits the direct form for `formats` and the copy form for `speech` in the same prologue. Their source declarations differed in exactly three ways, and all three were probed:
PROBE 1 - THE CAST. `extern u8 sSpeechNameBuf[];` +
  `register SpeechBlock* speech = (SpeechBlock*)sSpeechNameBuf;`
  -> `extern SpeechBlock sSpeechNameBuf;` +
  `register SpeechBlock* speech = &sSpeechNameBuf;`
  (SpeechBlock typedef moved above the extern; the three sibling   sites `s32* T = (s32*)sSpeechNameBuf;` in fn_8009DE88,   fn_8009DF7C and fn_8009E08C respelled to `(s32*)&sSpeechNameBuf`).   47 changed lines. VERDICT NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, object hash   32009720a077 - byte-identical TU-wide, so no sibling moved   either. `formats` has no cast; the cast is NOT the   discriminator.
PROBE 2 - DECLARATION ORDER of the two initialised register   pointers:
  BEFORE: register SpeechBlock* speech = ...;
          register char* formats = lbl_80114A48;
  AFTER:  register char* formats = lbl_80114A48;
          register SpeechBlock* speech = ...;
  VERDICT NEUTRAL, and the aligned view at 0x28:0x48 is   instruction-for-instruction UNCHANGED: speech still lands in   r26 via r0 and formats still lands direct. Position among the   two pointers is NOT the discriminator.
PROBE 3 - STORAGE CLASS on the formals:
  `void AudioSetupBossStreams(register int idx, register char* name)`
  -> `void AudioSetupBossStreams(int idx, char* name)`
  VERDICT NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, object hash 32009720a077. MWCC   ignores `register` on these formals entirely, so the fact that   our build homes the formal idx in r31 while the target homes it   in r25 is not reachable through the storage class.
All three discarded; src/game/sound/sounds_evt.c is byte-unchanged from HEAD.

verifiers_run: NONE WERE RUN, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING: no verifier can be reached on this function, so a verifier list would misdescribe the screen. The instruction COUNTS DIFFER (target 826, ours 827) and every shipped stage is defined over a bijection between the two streams' words, so the refusal is decided before any verifier is invoked, per claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-a-count-asymmetric-residual and claim.law.DP_a-permutation-class-lead-on-a-count-asymmetric-function-is-refuted-by-its-own-signature-before-any-build. Explicitly NOT RUN and why: copy_register_fields and verify_consistent_recolor (no position-consistent renaming exists between 826 and 827 words); verify_value_equality_recolor (same, and it is a recolor mode, not a count mode); instruction_permutation and permute_instruction_atoms (a permutation is a bijection on one stream's atoms and there is no 827->826 bijection); verify_relocation_binding and unproven_recolor_audit (both are downstream of a stage that never starts). webfrank_audit.py reports nothing for this TU, which per claim.law.RQ_webfrank-audit-silence-is-not-ineligibility is no-opinion rather than a verdict - the verdict here is the count, which is why this record quotes it as 826/827 rather than N/N. THE ONLY THING THAT REOPENS THE POSTPROCESSOR PATH IS THE COUNT REACHING PARITY; until then the question is a source question and this record is about source.
